newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Rising China magnesium prices hit exports.
newsitem.headline: Rising China magnesium prices hit exports.

text.p: Rising magnesium prices in China since the beginning of the year have hit exports as international markets have softened, the general manager of a Chinese magnesium factory said on Monday.

"Between January and March this year, the price of magnesium in China has increased by 1,000-1,500 yuan ($120-180) per tonne," Minhe Magnesium Factory Import and Export general manager, Li Xiaoying, told Reuters.
The current price of magnesium ingots was about 21,000 yuan ($2,530) per tonne, Li, who was attending a week-long China non-ferrous metals fair in Hong Kong, said.
"If international prices are going down and it's not China's contribution, since China's production is going down, somebody else must be producing (and exporting) a lot of magnesium," Li said.
"The price of magnesium has to hit at least $2,800 per tonne before those smaller factories can make a profit," Li said.
Minhe Magnesium Factory, in southwestern Qinghai province, had received government support to expand its production capacity. The government is willing to prop up more successful factories, Li said.
Minhe planned to expand its magnesium production capacity from the current 4,000 tonnes per year to 7,000 tonnes per year by the end of 1997, Li said.
In the boom years of 1994 and 1995, when magnesium exports were skyrocketing, hundreds of small plants opened up to produce magnesium, Li said.
By the end of 1995, about 500-600 magnesium plants were in operation in China, exporting large amounts overseas.
Magnesium prices started weakening by the end of 1995 and by the last quarter of 1996, almost 90-95 percent of the factories had shut down, Li said.
Now, only a few big plants were in operation and domestic market stocks were low, contributing to the high prices, Li said.
"There may be a few Japanese-run factories, those who move their production to China, that are still in operation," Li said.
